post_insight:
What it is: A top-down carousel of the pastry kitchen’s signature chocolate dessert, plated on bone china over dark walnut.
Why it worked: The tight overhead crop and single hero dish read as craft, not marketing — 65.7× the usual likes even with quiet comments, so it travelled on saves and shares.
Try this: Shoot one hero dish top-down on a clean, high-contrast surface and let the plating carry the frame — no on-image text.

What it is: A photo of a woman in a sequinned dress standing in the glass-edged infinity pool, shot from behind as she looks out over the Palm Jumeirah islands and coastline.
Why it worked: The corner-glass vantage point turns the pool wall into a framing device for the view, and the styling contrast — a shimmering dress submerged in water against the aerial coastline — gives the eye two competing points of interest, which likely drove the 18.6× spike over this hotel's usual engagement.
Try this: Shoot future pool content from the glass-edge corner so the infinity wall doubles as a natural frame for the destination view.

What it is: A twilight photograph of Atlantis, The Royal's fanned-out tower facades with its choreographed fountain display firing in the foreground pool, captioned with the hotel's brand tagline.
Why it worked: The dusk lighting and mid-eruption fountain timing capture the building's signature architectural silhouette and its water feature simultaneously, giving a single frame more visual density and colour contrast (pink sky, warm interior lights, white spray) than the hotel's typical posts, which likely drives the 44.4x lift in engagement.
Consider this: Schedule and shoot the fountain show at the same blue-hour window again, framing the full facade so architecture and water feature both read clearly in one still.
